models.title: Observed nominal-minus-inflation-linked yield spread
models.summary: The reading compares nominal and inflation-protected yields to obtain an inflation-compensation proxy and cautions that other market factors affect it.

relationship.original_equation: Implied inflation compensation=nominal bond yield - inflation-protected bond yield
relationship.translation_notes: Both yields are decimal fractions on a shared annual convention; subtraction returns a decimal yield spread. No positive-only guard is imposed because observed compensation can be negative. Owner-PDF locator is retained on the project-derivation citation; the relationship source is the accessible corroboration.

variables.definition: Observed inflation-compensation yield difference, which is not pure expected inflation
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

assumptions: Source assumption: matched currency, issuer credit, maturity and yield/compounding conventions.
Source assumption: quoted inflation-linkage terms, lags and deflation protections are specified externally.
limitations: The spread includes inflation-risk and relative-liquidity effects and therefore cannot be labeled a pure inflation expectation.
The simple yield difference is a market spread convention; it is not the exact one-period Fisher conversion already covered by engineering-finance--fisher-real-rate.

models.title: Required bank reserves for covered deposit liabilities
models.summary: Required reserves are the applicable reserve fraction of covered customer deposits.

relationship.original_equation: Required reserves = covered deposits * reserve requirement
relationship.locator: Section 27.4: 27-4-how-banks-create-money; exact subsection stated in evidence
relationship.translation_notes: Currency times a fraction gives currency. Zero reserve requirement is permitted for this accounting identity; it is outside the positive-ratio simple multiplier model. No present-day jurisdictional requirement is asserted. Owner-PDF locator is retained on the project-derivation citation; the relationship source is the accessible corroboration.

models.title: Simple limiting deposit multiplier under full redeposit
models.summary: The simple reciprocal-reserve multiplier is a maximum expansion under the stated absence of currency leakage and excess reserves.

relationship.locator: Section 27.4: 27-4-how-banks-create-money; exact subsection stated in evidence
relationship.translation_notes: The pure1 is one unit of reserves; ratio and multiplier are dimensionless. Geometric-series justification sums successive deposits with ratio1-requiredfraction; footnote3 explicitly qualifies the maximum. Required-reserve accounting is a dependency but the limiting multiplier requires these additional behavioral assumptions. Owner-PDF locator is retained on the project-derivation citation; the relationship source is the accessible corroboration.

variables.definition: Limiting total deposit expansion per unit of newly available reserves under the model
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

assumptions: Source assumption: banks retain exactly the same reserve fraction, lend all the rest and all proceeds are redeposited.
Source assumption: no cash leakage, excess reserve holdings, defaults or other lending constraints in this theoretical limiting chain.
limitations: Not a forecast of modern bank lending or a general policy-control rule. A zero reserve ratio does not imply an economically attainable infinite expansion.

models.title: Limiting total deposits supported by an initial reserve injection
models.summary: The limiting sum includes the original deposit and all subsequent redeposits under the simple reserve model.

relationship.original_equation: Total deposits = new initial deposit / reserve requirement
relationship.locator: Section 27.4: 27-4-how-banks-create-money; exact subsection stated in evidence
relationship.translation_notes: Derived from the source simple multiplier times the initial injection; currency divided by fraction gives currency. This output is an independently defined system-wide limiting deposit amount, unlike a single bank minimum required reserve. Quantity equation monetary turnover does not equate this model output with GDP growth. Owner-PDF locator is retained on the project-derivation citation; the relationship source is the accessible corroboration.

variables.definition: Limiting sum of deposits including the original injection, not additional lending alone
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

assumptions: Source assumption: injection adds reserves available to support deposits, rather than merely transferring an existing deposit between banks.
Source assumption: exactly the stated reserve fraction retained, full lending/redeposit, no cash leakage or other constraints.
limitations: Additional deposits beyond the original injection equal total-initial; do not call total itself incremental lending.
Observed monetary expansion can be much smaller and need not follow this limiting model.
